attribution.note: Marcus wrote the sentence himself in his own Substack essay. The Hinton and Musk quotes are only the targets of his remark.

semantics.note: This is a retrospective observation covering 2016 to March 2025. The normalised wording keeps the 'as far as I know' qualifier and the 'a single radiologist' threshold. It neither adds to nor drops from what he said.

contract.note: The contract keeps the knowledge qualifier and uses the ordinary meaning of replacement: losing a job or a whole role, not just automating tasks. Because of the qualifier, contradicting the claim would need proof of what Marcus knew. The contract correctly treats the claim as effectively untestable.

evidence.note: A December 2024 RSNA report describing radiologist shortages in academic departments. It is relevant background, but shortages can coexist with individual displacement, and it says nothing about Marcus's knowledge. It neither supports nor contradicts the claim.

reviews.rationale: 'As far as I know' turns the claim into a statement about Marcus's own knowledge, and no available record can test that. The frozen contract sets the axis to not_applicable. Contradiction would need a documented AI replacement plus evidence that Marcus knew of it, and no such evidence exists. The only item, an RSNA staffing report, is context. Not finding a replacement does not prove none happened. So the claim cannot be scored.
